seller_questions: Can you send the full VIN and a photo of the title showing it is clean and in your name?
Can you send a photo of the odometer with the car running, showing the exact mileage and no warning lights?
How long have you owned it, and how many owners did it have before you?
Has the car ever been on a track, at autocross, or at a drift event, by you or a previous owner?
Has the ECU ever been flashed or tuned (OFT, EcuTek, etc.) and returned to stock, or are headers, an intake or a different exhaust in the garage?
Do you have oil-change receipts or a dealer service printout? What oil and what interval did you use?
Is the clutch original? Any slipping, chatter, or a chirp or whine when the pedal is pressed?
What brand are the tires, and what are the four-digit DOT date codes on each?
Has the car had any paintwork or bodywork, including bumper respray or lip repair?
Will you provide a current smog certificate, and can I have an independent PPI done in the Merced/Atwater area before payment?
Can you send a cold-start video from fully cold, with the hood open?
ppi_focus: Read the ECU for flash or tune history and check readiness monitors and stored codes. Confirm a stock intake, headers and the cat/front pipe.
Compression and leakdown test, plus oil level and condition, to look for signs of track use or oil consumption.
Check the clutch engagement point and slip under load in a high gear, listen for throwout-bearing noise, and test synchro feel in 2nd and 3rd.
Check the underside for track or curb damage: front lip and undertray scrapes, subframe and pinch welds, and differential and transmission leaks.
Paint meter on the black panels, especially the front bumper, hood and quarters. Check panel gaps for prior collision repair.
Check suspension bushings, strut mounts and alignment specs; uneven tire wear would suggest past lowering or hard use.
Read tire DOT codes and tread depth on all four. Measure brake pad and rotor thickness and check brake fluid condition.
Listen for cold-start idle and FA20 injector tick and check for any valve-spring-recall-style noise. Check for open recalls by VIN.
Check the seat belts, airbag light and SRS codes, and match the door-jamb VIN label to the title.
what_would_change_verdict: Up: the VIN is supplied with a clean history report (no accidents, consistent odometer, few owners) and service receipts showing regular oil changes.
Up: a clean PPI showing a stock ECU, good compression and leakdown, a healthy clutch, a dry underside and recent-date tires.
Down: the seller refuses the VIN or a PPI, or the history report shows an accident, branded title or odometer inconsistency.
Down: evidence of a flashed ECU, headers, track use, or a worn or slipping clutch.
evidence.mission_note: A manual, naturally aspirated 86 at $18,500 in California fits the enthusiast-bridge brief squarely on spec, budget and resale. Whether it is a good bridge depends entirely on confirming its use history and identity, because nothing beyond the photos is documented yet.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes, through photos, a black first-generation Toyota 86 with a 6-speed manual, factory-looking wheels, exhaust and ride height, and California plates. The clean title, 'completely stock' status and 57,XXX miles are seller assertions only: there is no VIN, no history report, no service records, and the odometer is masked. Observed condition is ordinary for the mileage; the interior shows light-to-moderate wear, so the 'like new' label is not supported. The model's key risks are all unanswered: track or autocross use, ECU tune history, clutch condition, accident history and tire age. The $18,500 ask is within the fair-value band of $16,468–$19,753, slightly above the $17,745 mid, and below the active 86 asks. Logistics are favourable, since Atwater is a short in-state drive and the car is already California-registered, but PPI access has not been confirmed.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller for the full VIN, an odometer photo with the engine running, and confirmation that an independent PPI before payment is acceptable. Then run a history report on the VIN.
